about: Please Sir, May I Have Some More shows a small, scruffy blond boy in a rough brown workhouse tunic holding out an empty metal bowl with both hands, a spoon resting in it, while rows of other boys sit at long tables behind him. His face is timid and pleading. It is the famous scene from Oliver Twist where the starving orphan dares to ask for a second helping of gruel and causes an uproar. As a meme it captions a nervous, humble request for a little more of something you have clearly been rationed: memory, budget, time, sleep or attention.
origin: The scene comes from Charles Dickens' novel Oliver Twist, first published as a serial in 1837 to 1839, where Oliver asks the workhouse master "Please, sir, I want some more." The image is a still from one of the many screen adaptations; the meme usually softens the line to "may I have some more".
usage:
The top box is usually "please sir", and the bottom box finishes the request: "may I have some more ___". You can also put the stingy authority figure's offer in the top box and the plea in the bottom.

The best captions ask for something small that is weirdly hard to get: more RAM, a bigger budget, a deadline extension, one more life in a game, more episodes of a cancelled show. The meeker the wording, the better it matches Oliver's face.
ideas: may I have some more ram
may I have a deadline extension
may I have one more life
please sir, may I have some more tasks
may I have 5 more minutes of sleep
aka: Please Sir, I Want Some More
Please Sir, May I Have Some More
